banned_anti_patterns.ban: Client-provided data (via POST body or query params) MUST NOT be used as authoritative for purchase_amount, seat_allocation, or revenue attribution. All such fields MUST originate from backend order/ledger systems (ORD-1, LED-1).
banned_anti_patterns.enforcement_layer: Runtime policy + audit gate (OBS-1 audit log) + ORD-1/LED-1 purchase truth MUST come from backend.
banned_anti_patterns.rationale: Client data can be spoofed via browser dev tools or HTTP interception; treating it as truth breaks financial integrity and seat allocation correctness.

banned_anti_patterns.ban: Raw PII (email, phone, IP address, device_id, full user agent) MUST NOT be included in tracking event payloads. Only pseudonymous identifiers (subject_key via uuid_v7) and sanitized/hashed fields are permitted.
banned_anti_patterns.enforcement_layer: Schema validation + sanitization layer + lint gate (forbid PII patterns in test data).
banned_anti_patterns.rationale: Raw PII in tracking violates GDPR/CCPA minimization principles and creates compliance risk; pseudonymous identifiers allow analytics without PII exposure.

banned_anti_patterns.ban: Synchronous third-party dispatch (HTTP calls to GA4, Facebook Pixel, etc.) in checkout or payment flow is FORBIDDEN. All third-party dispatch MUST be async via DP-1 outbox.
banned_anti_patterns.enforcement_layer: Code review + PSC-1 latency budgets (checkout p99 ≤ 900ms cannot include external HTTP calls) + DP-1 outbox enforcement.
banned_anti_patterns.rationale: Sync dispatch blocks checkout on third-party availability; creates revenue risk if vendor is slow/down. Async via outbox ensures checkout completes regardless of vendor state.

banned_anti_patterns.ban: TRK-1 ingestion or dispatch logic MUST NOT bypass CONSENT-1 v1.1.0 evaluation. CONSENT-1 is the sole authority for consent state with cryptographic proof requirements (consent_evaluation_hash_sha256); no 'skip consent' flags or unconditional dispatch permitted.
banned_anti_patterns.enforcement_layer: Lint gate (verify CONSENT-1 v1.1.0 in dependencies) + structural gate (verify dispatch actions reference CONSENT-1 proof-hash check) + runtime consent_evaluation_hash_sha256 verification + manual code review.
banned_anti_patterns.rationale: Bypassing consent violates GDPR/CCPA; regulatory penalties + reputational damage. CONSENT-1 v1.1.0 centralization with proof-hash ensures consistent, auditable enforcement.

banned_anti_patterns.ban: TRK-1 tracking events (page_view, add_to_cart, etc.) MUST NOT be emitted via EVT-1 outbox. EVT-1 is for low-volume domain events (order finalized, ledger posted); high-volume tracking uses dedicated ingestion pipeline.
banned_anti_patterns.enforcement_layer: EVT-1 contract forbids tracking event types + lint gate (forbid ticketing.tracking.* in EVT-1 event registry).
banned_anti_patterns.rationale: Mixing high-volume tracking with low-volume domain events saturates EVT-1 outbox, breaks SLOs, and violates separation of concerns.

dedupe_key_rules.description: Attribution capture records are idempotent per subject for a bounded window; do not dedupe behavioral events.
notes: attribution_set_hash_sha256 is computed from a canonical JSON of utm_* + click ids (gclid/fbclid/ttclid) + referrer_domain + landing_path.
This preserves multiple event views across sessions while avoiding repeated attribution overwrites.

sanitization_rules.notes: Any field matching PII deny pattern MUST be stripped before storage and logged as ERR_TRK_PII_DETECTED.

async_only_rule.rationale: Sync dispatch blocks checkout on third-party availability; violates PSC-1 budgets and creates revenue risk.
async_only_rule.rule: Synchronous third-party dispatch in checkout or payment flow is FORBIDDEN. All dispatch MUST be async via DP-1 outbox pattern.

audit_logs.rule: Every dispatch attempt (success or failure) MUST be logged to audit table. Audit logs MUST include payload hash (SHA256) and consent_evaluation_hash_sha256 for forensic verification and consent audit trails.

consent_gating.notes: CONSENT-1 v1.1.0 introduces consent_evaluation_hash_sha256 (SHA-256 over canonicalized consent_evaluation per CANON-1). TRK-1 MUST verify proof-hash before dispatch to prevent consent bypass.

proof_requirement.rationale: CONSENT-1 v1.1.0 proof model ensures consent decisions are cryptographically auditable and non-repudiable; prevents bypass attacks.
proof_requirement.verification: Dispatch actions MUST include consent_evaluation_hash_sha256 from CONSENT-1 v1.1.0 proving consent was evaluated server-side per deterministic resolution algorithm.

consent_gating.rule: All third-party dispatch (GA4, Facebook Pixel, TikTok Pixel, etc.) MUST be gated by CONSENT-1 v1.1.0 evaluation with cryptographic proof (consent_evaluation_hash_sha256). If consent is denied or unknown, dispatch MUST NOT occur. No bypass paths permitted.

dispatch_flow_state_machine.proof_verification_step: Before dispatch, verify consent_evaluation_hash_sha256 exists and matches CONSENT-1 v1.1.0 canonical hash format (64-char hex lowercase SHA-256).

payload_allowlist_enforcement.rule: Only vendor-specific allowlisted fields MAY be dispatched to each vendor. Unlisted fields MUST be stripped before dispatch.

subcodes.reason: Consent evaluation returned false; dispatch/collection blocked per CONSENT-1 v1.1.0.
subcodes.remediation: Prompt user to grant consent; link to privacy settings.

subcodes.reason: consent_evaluation_hash_sha256 missing from dispatch request; CONSENT-1 v1.1.0 proof requirement not met.
subcodes.remediation: Call CONSENT-1 evaluation endpoint; include consent_evaluation_hash_sha256 in dispatch payload; do not bypass.

subcodes.reason: consent_evaluation_hash_sha256 format invalid (not 64-char hex lowercase SHA-256) or verification failed.
subcodes.remediation: Verify proof-hash generation uses CANON-1 canonicalization + SHA-256; check for tampering.

subcodes.reason: Event payload failed schema validation (missing required field, invalid type, etc.).
subcodes.remediation: Log validation error; correct payload and retry.

subcodes.reason: Event payload exceeds max size limit (8192 bytes).
subcodes.remediation: Truncate or split payload; retry with smaller payload.

subcodes.reason: Ingestion rate limit exceeded for tenant (org_id).
subcodes.remediation: Back off; implement exponential retry; escalate if sustained.

subcodes.reason: Vendor ID not in dispatch allowlist.
subcodes.remediation: Check vendor allowlist config; request vendor addition if needed.

subcodes.reason: Dispatch attempt failed (vendor unreachable, timeout, 5xx response, etc.).
subcodes.remediation: Log attempt; retry via DP-1 outbox with exponential backoff; escalate if repeated failures.

subcodes.reason: PII pattern detected in payload; event dropped/sanitized per AP-TRK-RAW-PII.
subcodes.remediation: Audit payload sanitization logic; flag for security review.

subcodes.reason: Event name doesn't match allowed taxonomy or namespace (must be ticketing.tracking.*).
subcodes.remediation: Check event name against contract taxonomy; correct and retry.

field_definitions.description: Tenant identifier; immutable; used for RLS and tenant sealing.
field_definitions.name: org_id

field_definitions.description: Client-reported timestamp (microsecond precision); server may adjust for clock skew.
field_definitions.name: occurred_at_utc

field_definitions.description: Pseudonymous identifier; uuid_v7(org_id + user_email + salt); hex lowercase 64 chars.
field_definitions.name: subject_key

field_definitions.description: Per-session temporal identifier; random UUIDv7; lifetime ≤ 1440 minutes (24h).
field_definitions.name: session_key

field_definitions.description: Google Click ID
field_definitions.name: gclid

field_definitions.description: Facebook Click ID
field_definitions.name: fbclid

field_definitions.description: Microsoft Click ID
field_definitions.name: msclkid

field_definitions.description: Price in minor currency units (cents); tracking metadata only; ORD-1 is authoritative.

field_definitions.description: References ORD-1 order record.
field_definitions.name: order_id

field_definitions.description: Payment transaction ID (if applicable).
field_definitions.name: transaction_id

field_definitions.description: Revenue in minor currency units; tracking metadata only; LED-1 is authoritative.
field_definitions.name: revenue_minor

field_definitions.description: Identifier for a specific occurrence/session within an event (EVT-2 occurrence). Required when the event supports multi-occurrence purchase or session-level attendance.

field_definitions.description: Identifier for the event content revision (EVT-2) rendered to the user at the time of the event.

event_taxonomy.naming_rule: All tracking events MUST be prefixed with 'ticketing.tracking.' namespace. Format: ticketing.tracking.<event_name>. Use snake_case for event names.

registry.description: User viewed a page (event detail page, checkout page, etc.).
User viewed an event or ticket product detail page.
User added item(s) to cart or initiated seat hold.
Purchase completed successfully. Revenue attribution source of truth is ORD-1/LED-1; this is behavioral tracking only.
registry.notes: Revenue fields are tracking metadata only; ORD-1 order snapshot is authoritative for financial reconciliation.

registry.description: Client-defined custom event (e.g., video play, form submit). Subject to same consent + PII + sanitization rules.
Records that a subject was exposed to an experiment variant on a specific surface for an event landing experience.

Emitted when an offer is visible to the public but purchase is blocked because eligibility requirements (entitlements) are not met. Used for funnel and upsell analytics; enforcement is still server-side in ORD-1.

event_taxonomy.versioning_rule: Event schema uses semantic versioning. New optional fields = minor version bump. Field removal or type change = major version bump. Backward compat: old field names MUST remain supported for 90 days after deprecation.

cross_device_rules.notes: Cross-device identity resolution (linking subject_keys across devices) requires explicit 'analytics' consent grant. Default: treat each device as separate subject_key.

identity_and_keys.explicit_no_pii_rule: Tracking payloads MUST NOT contain: email, phone, IP address (except hashed with daily salt rotation), full user agent (hash only), device_id (use session_key), postal_code, or any field matching PII deny patterns.

session_key.notes: Session boundary defined by: explicit logout, 24h timeout, or consent withdrawal.

subject_key.derivation: uuid_v7(org_id + subject_source_id + salt) where subject_source_id is chosen as: (1) anon_sticky_id (UUIDv7 random, first-party cookie) if present; else (2) actor_id (UUIDv7 from IAM-1) when authenticated.
notes: Subject keys MUST be pseudonymous and MUST NOT be derived from direct PII (email, phone, name).
anon_sticky_id is generated server-side at first consented analytics touch and persisted as a first-party cookie (suggested TTL: 180 days) to support cross-session attribution.
If CONSENT-1 denies analytics consent, anon_sticky_id MUST NOT be set/read; tracking events MUST be dropped or reduced to strictly-necessary operational telemetry.
Cross-device matching is out-of-scope for TRK-1 (no fingerprinting).

backpressure_and_failure.drop_behavior: If buffer exceeds capacity, drop oldest non-purchase events first; log drop count as ticketing.trk1.events.dropped.total metric.
backpressure_and_failure.notes: Tracking failures MUST NOT propagate to checkout response. Use fire-and-forget async ingestion with bounded buffer.
backpressure_and_failure.rule: Tracking ingestion MUST degrade (drop or buffer) without blocking checkout or payment flows. PSC-1 budgets: checkout p99 ≤ 900ms; tracking ingestion p99 ≤ 100ms.

idempotency.notes: If same (org_id, event_id) seen within 7 days, return success (idempotent replay) unless payload hash differs (conflict).

ingestion_guarantees.immutability: Tracking events are immutable after insert; no updates permitted except DSAR deletion.

multi_tenant_sealing.rationale: Per TEN-1 v1.7.0: org_id MUST be explicit in every write; no ambient/global tenant state.

alerting_rules.notes: Missing consent proofs indicate bypass attempt or integration bug.

break_glass_conditions: If drop rate > 5%, pause dispatch to vendors and page on-call (P1 incident).
If CONSENT-1 unavailable, default to eu_strict (deny tracking); alert immediately.
If consent proof verification failures > 10/min, trigger P0 alert (potential bypass attack or integration bug).

degradation_modes.action: Drop oldest non-purchase events; sample 10% if sustained.
Circuit-break vendor; queue for retry via DP-1.
Halt all dispatch; page security on-call (P0); investigate bypass attempt.

checkout_blocking_forbidden.rule: Tracking ingestion MUST NOT block checkout. If tracking fails, checkout MUST succeed. Drop tracking event and log error.

degraded_modes.buffer_overflow: Drop oldest non-purchase events; sampling 10% if sustained overflow.
degraded_modes.consent_service_unavailable: Default to eu_strict (deny tracking) per CONSENT-1 v1.1.0 locked_decisions.resolution_rule (most_restrictive_wins).
degraded_modes.vendor_dispatch_unavailable: Queue for retry via DP-1; do not block ingestion.

aggregate_retention.notes: Aggregates MUST NOT contain subject_key, session_key, or any re-identifiable fields.
aggregate_retention.rationale: Aggregated/anonymized attribution data may be retained longer for trend analysis (2 years).

dsar_deletion_hooks.aggregate_handling: Aggregates MAY remain if non-identifying (no subject_key); otherwise delete.
dsar_deletion_hooks.audit_trail: Log deletion completion in ARCH-1 audit log.
dsar_deletion_hooks.deletion_scope: All raw tracking events where subject_key matches DSAR subject_id.
dsar_deletion_hooks.timeline: Complete deletion within 30 days of DSAR request approval.

legal_hold_interaction.release_behavior: Resume normal retention policy after legal hold release.
legal_hold_interaction.rule: If legal hold active (ARCH-1), raw events MUST NOT be deleted even after retention period expires.

raw_event_retention.purge_behavior: Delete raw events after 90 days unless legal hold active (ARCH-1).
raw_event_retention.rationale: Per DATA-1 v2.0.3: operational data baseline is 90 days. Raw tracking events are operational (not long-term analytical).

invariants.statement: Tracking event taxonomy MUST be non-empty and contain all required event types (page_view, view_item, add_to_cart, begin_checkout, purchase).

invariants.enforcement: CI gate TRK-1-GATE-CONSENT-AUTHORITY (structural check: CONSENT-1 v1.1.0 in dependencies + dispatch actions reference consent_evaluation_hash_sha256 proof).
invariants.statement: CONSENT-1 v1.1.0 is the sole authority for consent evaluation with cryptographic proof requirements. TRK-1 ingestion and dispatch MUST NOT bypass CONSENT-1 v1.1.0 evaluation or proof verification (consent_evaluation_hash_sha256).

invariants.enforcement: Sanitization layer + lint gate TRK-1-GATE-PII-BAN-ENFORCEMENT (forbid PII patterns in test data).
invariants.statement: Tracking events MUST be pseudonymous by default. subject_key MUST be uuid_v7 derived; raw PII (email, phone, IP, device_id) MUST NOT be in payloads.
Tracking ingestion MUST degrade without blocking checkout. If buffer overflows or ingestion fails, drop events and log; checkout MUST succeed.
Third-party dispatch MUST be async via DP-1 outbox. Synchronous HTTP calls to vendors in checkout flow are FORBIDDEN.

invariants.enforcement: TEN-1 compliance gate + DB schema (org_id immutable constraint).
invariants.statement: org_id is immutable after tracking event creation. Cross-tenant queries MUST return ERR_NOT_FOUND (hide-existence per TEN-1).

invariants.enforcement: Audit schema gate TRK-1-GATE-DISPATCH-GOVERNANCE (verify audit log schema includes consent_evaluation_hash_sha256).
invariants.statement: All dispatch attempts (success or failure) MUST be logged to immutable audit table with payload_hash, consent_evaluation_hash_sha256, vendor_id, timestamp, result.

invariants.enforcement: Runtime proof verification gate + OBS-1 alert (ticketing.trk1.consent.proof_missing.total > 10/min triggers P0 incident).
invariants.statement: Dispatch actions MUST verify consent_evaluation_hash_sha256 format (64-char hex lowercase SHA-256) before dispatch. Missing or invalid proof MUST surface ERR_TRK_CONSENT_PROOF_MISSING or ERR_TRK_CONSENT_PROOF_INVALID.

never_owns: Business intelligence definitions, dashboards, or aggregation logic (BI-1)
Domain truth for orders, ledger, or seat allocation (ORD-1, LED-1, SEAT-1)
Consent evaluation logic (CONSENT-1 is sole authority)
Third-party tag injection or client-side tracking libraries (client responsibility)
out_of_scope: A/B testing framework (future contract if needed)
Cross-device identity resolution without explicit consent
owns: Canonical tracking event taxonomy (page_view, view_item, add_to_cart, begin_checkout, purchase, custom_event)
Ingestion rules: append-only, idempotent, tenant-sealed, backpressure/drop rules
Consent-gated collection and dispatch (CONSENT-1 v1.1.0 is sole authority; bypass forbidden; proof-hash required)
Attribution capture: UTM params, click IDs, referrer; sanitization, dedupe, normalization
Third-party dispatch governance: vendor allowlist, payload allowlist, rate limits, audit logs, async-only
Raw tracking retention and DSAR deletion hooks
Performance safety: tracking MUST degrade without blocking checkout

rules.text: Event taxonomy registry MUST be non-empty and MUST contain all required event types with stable snake_case names prefixed with ticketing.tracking.*

Consent-gated dispatch flow MUST evaluate CONSENT-1 v1.1.0 and verify consent_evaluation_hash_sha256 before every third-party HTTP call; if consent denied, proof missing, or proof invalid, drop dispatch and log appropriate error code.
Attribution dedupe key (org_id + subject_key + utm_source + utm_medium + utm_campaign) MUST be unique within 7-day window; duplicates silently ignored (idempotent).
Sanitization MUST strip any field matching PII deny patterns (email, phone, password, SSN) before storage; log ERR_TRK_PII_DETECTED and reject event.
Raw tracking event retention is 90 days (operational tier per DATA-1); DSAR deletion MUST purge all events where subject_key matches within 30 days.
consent_evaluation_hash_sha256 MUST be 64-character hexadecimal lowercase string (SHA-256 output format); any other format MUST be rejected with ERR_TRK_CONSENT_PROOF_INVALID.

summary: Defines canonical first-party tracking event taxonomy, consent-gated ingestion and third-party dispatch with cryptographic proof requirements (CONSENT-1 v1.1.0), attribution capture and normalization, retention and deletion hooks, and performance safety guarantees. TRK-1 governs behavioral tracking only—NOT business intelligence (BI-1), operational telemetry (OBS-1), or domain truth (ORD-1/LED-1). Platform-authoritative for tracking governance.

tenancy.rationale: Per TEN-1 v1.7.0 Constitutional Invariant TEN-INV-HIDE-EXIST: org_id is immutable after creation; cross-tenant queries return ERRNOTFOUND (not ERRFORBIDDEN); RLS enforced at DB layer.
